title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This sits in the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets', the continuation of La Longue Marche. Grothendieck is solving an equation in a rank-2 linear group (GL2/SL2, apparently over F_ℓ or a base where F_ℓ-points matter). Equation (1) has roughly the shape [α,ρ] = [β,σ]·ε1(ν), where ρ and σ are fixed elements, α, β and ν are unknowns, and ε1 is a fixed homomorphism into a unipotent group L1. This is the kind of relation one gets when counting or parametrising homomorphisms from a surface-type fundamental group (a relation built from commutators, i.e. loops) into GL2.

On the previous page he proposed a parametrisation (2):
- Start from a Borel-type group B'_0 and the centralisers T_ρ, T_σ.
- Send (u, a, b) to α = u·a', β = u·b' and the third unknown v(u). Concretely α = u a^{-1}, β = u b^{-1}, as in (10) on the next page.
- He showed that the key condition for (2) to give solutions is σ^{-1}ρ ∈ Γ B_0, i.e. ρ(B'_0) = σ(B'_0).

This page continues in three steps.

(i) Non-uniqueness. The fibres of (2) are orbits of the right action (u, a, b) ↦ (ut, at, bt), where t is a point of T_ρ ∩ T_σ ∩ B'_0. Hence the earlier wish (5) that this intersection be trivial.

(ii) Surjectivity. Does every solution of (1) have the form (u a', u b', v(u))? For regular ρ and σ this reduces to the surjectivity of map (6), B'_0 → H_{ρ,σ}, u ↦ ([u,ρ], [u,σ], v(u)). Here H_{ρ,σ} is the scheme of triples (ξ, η, ν) satisfying (7): det ξ = det η = 1, Tr ξρ = Tr ρ, Tr ησ = Tr σ, ξ = η ε1(ν).
- The reduction works because a commutator ξ = gρg^{-1}ρ^{-1} automatically has det 1 and Tr(ξρ) = Tr ρ.
- Conversely, if ρ is regular and ξρ has the same characteristic polynomial as ρ, then (in the regular semisimple case, or when the two are conjugate) ξρ = gρg^{-1}. So ξ = [g,ρ], with g unique modulo T_ρ.
- The equation thus becomes a fibre-type problem: realise simultaneously both 'twisted conjugacy classes' by a single g ranging over B'_0.

(iii) The draconian hypotheses. He recalls that the strong hypotheses of section II (pp. 435–436) were made essentially to get this surjectivity. After a computation they amount to (8):
- (a) σ^{-1}ρ is a point of the unipotent radical L_0 = (B_0)_u and is not central.
- (b) B_0 and B_1 = ρ(B_0) = σ(B_0) are in general position, i.e. L_0 and L_1 = ρ(L_0) = σ(L_0) are independent (opposite/transversal unipotent radicals).

He states openly that it is unclear whether these conditions, suggested by earlier and heavier computations, are really indispensable for the parametrisation result.

The next page goes on: (a) is natural (σ^{-1}ρ unipotent or quasi-unipotent), (b) is 'imprévisible'. He then passes to a twisted equation (9) with ε = −1 and Tr σ = 0, aiming at the isomorphism (10), B'_0 × T_ρ × N'_σ ≅ G*_{ρ,σ}.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. Two caveats on the reduction to (6). First, 'Tr ξρ = Tr ρ and det ξ = 1' implies ξρ conjugate to ρ only when ρ is regular semisimple, or regular with ξρ also regular; in the non-semisimple case one needs regularity of ξρ too. Grothendieck covers this only by '(si ρ, σ sont régulières)'. Second, the conjugating element g must be shown to lie in B'_0, not merely in G, which is exactly where conditions (8) enter. The surjectivity question is explicitly left open; the page does not decide whether (8) is necessary.

ideas.what: Parametrising solutions of a commutator equation [α,ρ] = [β,σ]·ε1(ν) by (u, a, b) ∈ B'_0 × T_ρ × T_σ, with fibres given by torsors under T_ρ ∩ T_σ ∩ B'_0
ideas.modern_name: Explicit parametrisation of components of character/representation varieties of surface-type groups in SL2/GL2, via twisted conjugacy classes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Representation-variety computations in general (Goldman, Fricke–Klein-type trace coordinates); this specific setup is not attributed
ideas.where_published: Unpublished (cote 140-3, sequel to La Longue Marche)

ideas.what: Reducing surjectivity to the map g ↦ ([g,ρ],[g,σ]) onto the scheme defined by det = 1 and Tr ξρ = Tr ρ (the commutator map onto the 'trace-fixed' locus)
ideas.modern_name: Image of the commutator map / Steinberg-type fibres of the conjugation map g ↦ gρg^{-1}ρ^{-1}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard linear algebraic group theory (Steinberg, Kostant on regular elements)

ideas.what: Sufficient conditions (8): σ^{-1}ρ non-central in the unipotent radical of B_0, and B_0, ρ(B_0) in general position (opposite Borels)
ideas.modern_name: Opposite Borel subgroups / Bruhat big cell condition

missed.claim: Grothendieck leaves open whether the 'draconian' general-position hypotheses (8) are necessary for surjectivity of the parametrisation (2)/(6) of solutions of the loop equation, i.e. whether every solution comes from B'_0. This is an explicitly stated, unresolved question.
missed.quote: mais il n'est pas clair si ces conditions (suggérées par des calculs antérieurs ...) sont vraiment indispensables pour le résultat de paramétrisation
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It is a concrete linear-algebra question about rank-2 representation varieties, likely solvable by a Bruhat-decomposition case analysis. It matters only as part of the unexplored programme of the 'équation des lacets' notes.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working page of technical SL2/GL2 computations. Its main content is a reduction of a surjectivity question to a trace/commutator scheme, plus an admitted doubt about earlier hypotheses. The ideas are standard; the only interest is the open question within an unpublished programme.
transcription_corrections: Header '486' is Grothendieck's own pagination; archive page 369.
First line of (8): 'ρσρ section de (B_0)_u = L_0 (où [?] pas centrale [?] de B_0)' should read 'σ^{-1}ρ section de (B_0)_u = L_0 (et pas centrale de B_0)'.
'Il revient au même (si ρ,σ sont régulières) de dire que la lie [?] à surjectivité de' is roughly 'il revient au même ... de demander la surjectivité de'; the struck-through word is a deletion.
'au prix de [?] un calcul' should read 'au prix d'un calcul'.

The final lines are garbled and duplicated in the transcription. They read approximately: 'mais il n'est pas clair si ces conditions (suggérées par des calculs antérieurs, et devenant [illegible] par des calculs plus lourds) sont vraiment indispensables pour le résultat de paramétrisation'.
In (6) the third component is v(u), underlined, matching (u a', u b', v(u)) above.
'ce qui [?] fibre [?])' is closer to 'ce qui ... fixe)'; uncertain.
